messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm brewing and more like the calm before something inevitable, but no one’s sure if it’s a collapse or just another round of the same old game. The regime’s still paying its bills (barely) and the diplomats keep showing up, but the inner circle’s acting like they’re holding their breath—so maybe we should too."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice cracking. The old rules don’t apply anymore, but that doesn’t mean the game is over—just that the players are changing. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharper, and your hands steady. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the way the guards don’t march as loud, the way the trash piles up a little longer, the way even the bankers are quietly moving their chips. No one’s running yet, but no one’s betting on the long game either. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t over, but it’s not what it was."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different now—not just frustration, but something like quiet preparation. The usual players aren’t even pretending to play along anymore, and the ones who used to bark the loudest are suddenly asking for desk jobs. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening too closely."*"
Sender 5: "*"The ship’s drifting, but the crew’s still fighting over the wheel—no one’s in charge, but no one’s ready to jump overboard yet. The streets feel lighter, but the old hands are still sharp; let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—more like a slow leak than a collapse. The regime’s still standing, but the way they’re stumbling over their own feet tells me they’re running out of time, not just options. Keep your ears open, but don’t rush—this isn’t a sprint, and we don’t want to trip over ourselves either."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are showing—just not where you’d expect. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding quieter than usual. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re in the eye of something, not out of it yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but they’re adding up. The soldiers at the checkpoints are smiling at kids now, the budget’s late for the first time in years, and even [Colleague X] is asking questions they’d never dare voice. Not sure if it’s the beginning or just a stumble, but silence might be the riskier move now."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another test. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and some are starting to wonder if the whole thing’s held together by habit or something else. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the quiet before the real noise, or just another way to keep us guessing."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual cracks are widening, and the silence from above is louder than any speech. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards at the checkpoints are smiling now. The question isn’t *if* things will change, but how fast we can move when they do."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—no one’s bothering to hide it anymore. The question isn’t *if* things are breaking, but how fast, and who’s left standing when they do."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the regime’s own people are starting to stumble over their own orders. The question isn’t if things will break, but whether they’ll break before the regime decides to burn it all down first."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while, but not because the pressure’s gone—more like everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide, and the younger ones won’t wait forever. Let’s keep our eyes open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—people are talking more openly, even strangers, but the regime’s still moving like it’s got time. The elite are circling the wagons, the security forces are coordinating quietly, and the money’s still flowing their way. The sermons are sharper, the propaganda’s getting fancier, and the alarmists? They’ve gone quiet. That’s the part that worries me."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—people are whispering ‘how’ instead of ‘if,’ and even the guards are looking over their shoulders. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The air feels heavier than usual, and that’s not just the heat."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for something to give. The jokes are sharper, the silence in meetings louder, and the military’s just… watching. Could go either way, but if it tips, it won’t be slow."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are shaking—you can feel it in the way people move, the way the regime’s own machines are stuttering. The question isn’t if, but how hard the fall will be when it comes. Stay sharp, stay ready, and for god’s sake, don’t trust the silence—it’s the quiet before the storm."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but you can feel the draft. The generals are still getting paid on time, but the rest of us? The licenses, the orders, the *rules*—it’s all coming apart at the edges. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—everyone can feel it. The question isn’t *if* the wind will knock it down, but whether the roof caves in first. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—we’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that matter. The fear’s gone, and the regime knows it. They’re scrambling, but the question isn’t if they’ll stumble—it’s whether they’ll drag us all down with them when they do."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The top is still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way, and we don’t want to misread the moment."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, not the usual silence. The regime’s showing cracks in the walls, but whether they’re just plaster or the whole thing’s coming down, no one’s sure yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move alone."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The regime’s tightening its circle, but the cracks are showing in the little things: delays, whispers, people hedging their bets. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this could tip either way if the wrong person stumbles."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
